tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name

- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.text:
Looked at the code and production data. The change is live: merged to main as PR #53, and `db:check` confirms migrations 00069 and 00070 are applied on production. (Note: 00071 and 00072 are **missing on production** — that's the separate submission-processing work, not this.)

## It's working, on real data

**Every application since the change is linked to an account.** 75 applications created since 23 Sep, all 75 with a `user_id`, 74 of them with a CV.

- **41** of those accounts were created by the apply flow itself (`registration.application_completed` = 41 in the event log)
- **34** used an account the person already had
- `application.submitted` = 76, with 1 deleted by an admin, which matches the 75

**The backfill and triggers hold across the whole history.** Of 1593 applications, 1272 are linked and 321 are not. All 321 are genuinely accountless legacy applicants: there are **zero** cases where a profile exists for the email but the link is missing, and no duplicate profiles sharing an email (which would leave a row deliberately unlinked).

**No leftover verification codes.** The `verification_codes` table is empty, so every code was consumed and deleted, and no encrypted passwords are sitting in storage. Worth knowing: nothing cleans up *abandoned* codes (no cron for it), so a dropped signup would leave a row with an encrypted password until it's consumed. Today there are none.

## Effects on the account

- **A brand-new account is signed in automatically** after applying. **An existing account is not** — the code proves the email but not the password, so a returning applicant lands on the confirmation page still logged out. Deliberate, but it surprises people.
- **Email is now an identity.** Migration 00070 stops participants from changing their own `profiles.email` through the API. Only `adminChangeUserEmail` (`lib/actions/admin.ts:1476`) can, as the service role.

## Stopping an application

**There's no self-service withdraw anywhere in the codebase.** An applicant who changes their mind has to email you. Two admin paths exist:

- **Delete** (`deleteApplication`) removes only the application row. The account stays, and the person can apply again since the per-chapter email uniqueness is freed. 1 deleted since 22 Sep.
- **Cancel** (`cancelApplication`) works only on `accepted` or `checked_in`, is terminal, and also leaves the account. 7 cancelled in total: 5 are legacy rows with no `cancelled_at` (cancelled before the action existed), 2 went through the proper action. No cancelled person is still sitting in a challenge roster, so that cleanup is working.

## One live bug this change introduced

**Two people cannot apply through the public form at all**: the mixed-case jury profiles from earlier, which were never normalized.

```
profile: Sebastian.BA.Baeuml@bmw-motorrad.de   auth: sebastian.ba.baeuml@bmw-motorrad.de
profile: J.effenberger@icloud.com              auth: j.effenberger@icloud.com
```

The apply flow looks the profile up with a case-sensitive match on the lowercased address (`lib/actions/applications.ts:288` and `:445`). For these two it misses, so they look like new users and are asked to set a password. Account creation then fails, because the auth user already exists, and they get "We could not create your account. Please try again." with no way through. Jury login itself is fine, since PR #116 made that lookup case-insensitive. The apply and walk-in paths (`lib/actions/walk-in.ts:160`) never got the same treatment.

Also worth tidying: `cancelApplication` still resolves the person by case-sensitive email (`:1070`) to clean up rosters, even though `app.user_id` is now right there. It works today because all 1593 application emails are lowercase, but it's redundant and would silently skip the roster cleanup on a case mismatch.

Want me to fix these? I'd do it as one PR: normalize the two profile rows, make the apply and walk-in lookups case-insensitive, and switch the cancel cleanup to `user_id`, with tests.
